text: This project uses pytest for all unit tests; test files live under tests/ and mirror the module they test.
We fixed a bug where retryOperation() swallowed the last exception instead of re-raising it after max attempts.
Architecture decision: use a Protocol class for DeciderClient so we can swap the mock scorer for a real Decider 2B backend later without touching callers.
Coding convention: prefer dataclasses over plain dicts for structured return values like Decision(label, confidence).
Bug fix: MemoryStore.load() used to crash on a single malformed JSON entry; now it logs a warning and skips just that entry.
Decision: curated memories are capped at MAX_MEMORIES=5 to keep Bedrock prompt size small and predictable.
Convention: environment variables are read once at module import time (e.g. BEDROCK_MODEL_ID) rather than scattered through the call stack.
Architecture decision: the CLI is a plain REPL loop with no web framework; python -m cli is the only supported entry point for the demo.
Bug fix: confidence scores above 1.0 were possible due to a double-counting token overlap bug in the mock scorer; clamped to [0, 1].
Convention: all Bedrock/AWS calls are wrapped in try/except and surfaced as a clear CLI error message; the REPL never crashes on an AWS error.
Decision: relevance threshold defaults to 0.6; memories scoring below this are excluded from the Bedrock context even if MAX_MEMORIES isn't reached.
Bug fix: the relevance table in the CLI was sorting by memory id instead of confidence descending; fixed to sort by confidence.
Convention: keep decider_client.py free of any Bedrock/Strands imports so the decision pattern stays reusable outside this project.
Architecture decision: memory_curator.py owns ranking and filtering; decider_client.py only scores one memory at a time and has no knowledge of ranking.
Bug fix: MockDeciderClient's simulated latency used time.sleep(0.115) on every call, which made batch scoring slow; now simulated once per curate() call via a single sleep.
Convention: JSON memory entries require id, text, tags (list), and created_at (ISO 8601 string); anything else is treated as malformed.
Decision: the CLI prints both a curated-vs-everything character count comparison and an estimated token count comparison, approximating tokens as characters / 4.
